set.acceptance: text-refs-display.txtar: after a node's statement refers to @other and other is renamed to renamed, rhiza show, why, slice, ls, tree, search, inbox, feed, roadmap, change show and change diff print @renamed wherever they print that statement, in markdown and in --json fields; rhiza search '@renamed' finds the node; rhiza render writes @renamed into the rendered page; a reference to a node not in the view shows @{<full ID>}; after other is retired the reference shows @{<other's full ID>} and writing the shown statement back with rhiza set stores the same text; a log entry written by hand before the feature with '@word' and '@{ID}' in a statement shows '@@word' and '@@{ID}', and writing that back stores the same literal text; a statement written with '@@word' stores a literal @word and is shown as @@word; copying the shown text into rhiza set stores the same text (same IDs, literal @ kept literal)
set.statement: Every read operation that prints a node's text fields (render, show, why, slice, ls, tree, search, inbox, feed, roadmap, change show and change diff, the last two in the change set's view), in text and --json alike, show each stored @{<26-character ID>} as @<the node's current handle> in that view when it names a live node, and as @{<full ID>} when it names a retired node or does not resolve there; search matches its query against this shown text; and show a stored literal @ that would start a reference as @@
